pharm: Recombinant glycoprotein that mimics endogenous erythropoietin, stimulating red blood cell production by promoting division and differentiation of erythroid progenitors in the bone marrow.
quick: Use only if clearly needed; use single-dose vials
Use single-dose vials; large molecule, limited transfer
Used in CKD anemia; titrate to lowest effective Hb
summary: Epoetin alfa is a recombinant human erythropoiesis-stimulating agent (ESA) used to treat anemia due to chronic kidney disease, zidovudine in HIV, and myelosuppressive chemotherapy, and to reduce allogeneic transfusion in elective non-cardiac, non-vascular surgery. It carries a boxed warning: ESAs increase the risk of death, myocardial infarction, stroke, venous thromboembolism, vascular-access thrombosis, and tumor progression or recurrence. Use the lowest dose needed to avoid RBC transfusions and do not target hemoglobin above the recommended range.
indications: Anemia due to chronic kidney disease in patients on dialysis and not on dialysis
Anemia due to zidovudine in patients with HIV infection
Anemia due to concomitant myelosuppressive chemotherapy with at least two additional months of planned chemotherapy
Reduction of allogeneic RBC transfusions in patients undergoing elective, noncardiac, nonvascular surgery

moa: Epoetin alfa is a recombinant form of human erythropoietin produced in mammalian cells. It binds the erythropoietin receptor on erythroid progenitor cells in the bone marrow, stimulating their proliferation, differentiation, and maturation into red blood cells and the release of reticulocytes into the circulation. This raises the hematocrit and hemoglobin, reducing the need for transfusions when adequate iron is available.

absolute: Pure red cell aplasia (PRCA) that begins after treatment with epoetin alfa or other erythropoietin protein drugs
Serious allergic reactions to epoetin alfa
Multidose formulation with benzyl alcohol in neonates, infants, pregnant women, and lactating women
relative: Active malignancy where cure is the anticipated outcome (chemotherapy use)

preg: There are limited data in pregnant women; use only if clearly needed, and use single-dose, benzyl-alcohol-free vials. Anemia management benefits should outweigh potential risks.
lact: It is not known whether epoetin alfa is excreted in human milk; as a large glycoprotein, systemic absorption by the infant is unlikely. Use single-dose preservative-free vials when breastfeeding.
renal: Epoetin alfa is a primary therapy for anemia of chronic kidney disease. Use the lowest dose sufficient to reduce the need for RBC transfusions; for CKD on dialysis, initiate ESA when hemoglobin is less than 10 g/dL and reduce or interrupt the dose if hemoglobin approaches or exceeds 11 g/dL.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment is established for hepatic impairment.

moderate: Concomitant ESAs or other agents that raise hemoglobin rapidly (additive thrombotic risk)
minor: No clinically significant pharmacokinetic drug interactions established
interactions.diagnostics: Raises hemoglobin/hematocrit and reticulocyte count; may increase platelet count early in therapy.

serious: Thromboembolic events (MI, stroke, DVT/PE, vascular-access thrombosis)

Serum Tmax ~5-24 hours after SC dosing

pearls: Boxed warning: ESAs raise risk of death, MI, stroke, thromboembolism, vascular-access thrombosis, and tumor progression
Use the lowest dose to avoid transfusions; do not target hemoglobin above the recommended range
Always assess and replete iron - ESA resistance is most often iron deficiency
New or worsening hypertension and seizures can occur with rapid hemoglobin rise
Investigate sudden loss of efficacy with low reticulocytes for antibody-mediated pure red cell aplasia
missed: Doses are scheduled by the care team; a missed dose should be given as soon as possible and the schedule resumed. Do not double doses to make up for a missed one.
overdose: Overdose can cause excessive erythropoiesis (polycythemia) and severe hypertension. Manage with phlebotomy if clinically indicated, hold therapy until hemoglobin falls into the target range, and provide blood-pressure control and supportive care.
